- Spiral galaxies: NGC 5457 (8.7), NGC 5474 (11.9)

The statement says: "irregular galaxy is the object type having 2.1 more apparent magnitude than spiral galaxy."  
This means the average (or typical) apparent magnitude of irregular galaxies should be 2.1 greater than that of spiral galaxies.

Calculate average apparent magnitude for irregular galaxies:

Calculate average apparent magnitude for spiral galaxies:  
(8.7 + 11.9) / 2 = 20.6 / 2 = 10.3

Difference: 14.25 − 10.3 = 3.95

The statement says 2.1 more, but the actual difference is 3.95, not 2.1.
